'''Joan Henri van der Waals''' (2 May 1920 – 21 June 2022) was a Dutch physicist. He was professor of experimental physics at [[Leiden University]] between 1967 and 1989. He specialized in molecular physics and [[clathrate hydrate]]s. One of Van der Waals's most significant contributions to the study of hydrates was a series of papers between 1953 and 1958, which eventually culminated in the 1959 publication of his paper on the canonical partition function for clathrates, along with J. C. Platteeuw. To create this partition function, van der Waals made a number of simplifying assumptions, most prominently that neighboring guest gas molecules cannot interact and there is a maximum of one guest per cage.

==Early life==
Van der Waals was born on 2 May 1920 in [[Amsterdam]].<ref name="KaaKaa2008">{{cite book|author1=D. J. van de Kaa|author2=Kaa|author3=Y. de Roo|title=De Leden Van de Koninklijke Nederlandse Akademie Van Wetenschappen: Een Demografisch Perspectief: 1808 Tot 2008|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=gzNvCGJEGCYC&pg=PA356|date=19 December 2008|publisher=Amsterdam University Press|isbn=978-90-6984-552-4|page=356}}</ref><ref name=ul>{{cite web|author= |url=https://hoogleraren.leidenuniv.nl/id/2702 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200502110512/https://hoogleraren.leidenuniv.nl/id/2702 |title=Joan Henri van der Waals |language=Dutch |publisher=Leiden University |date= |archive-date=2 May 2020}}</ref> A book on the [[Bohr model]] sparked his interest in physics.<ref name=mare/> After finishing his high school in Amsterdam he moved to [[London]] to work as an intern-apprentice in a laboratory. When he returned to the Netherlands he started a combined study of physics, chemistry and maths at the [[University of Amsterdam]]. With the [[Battle of the Netherlands|German invasion of the Netherlands in May 1940]], Van der Waals was called for military service for the mounted artillery. He was made [[prisoner of war]] but was allowed to return to his studies in June 1940.<ref name=nk>{{cite web|author= |url=https://www.nederlandsekrijgsmacht.nl/index.php/kl/301-eenheden-nederlandse-leger/herdenkingen/1108-joan-van-der-waals-symposium-ter-ere-van-zijn-95ste-verjaardag |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200502113439/https://www.nederlandsekrijgsmacht.nl/index.php/kl/301-eenheden-nederlandse-leger/herdenkingen/1108-joan-van-der-waals-symposium-ter-ere-van-zijn-95ste-verjaardag |title=2015. Joan van der Waals: symposium ter ere van zijn 95ste verjaardag |language=Dutch |publisher=nederlandskrijgsmacht.nl |date=14 May 2015 |archive-date=2 May 2020}}</ref> In 1942, Van der Waals completed the long-distance tour-skating event, the ''[[Elfstedentocht]]''.<ref name=mare/> In 1943 he refused to sign the {{Interlanguage link multi|Loyaliteitsverklaring|nl}} and went into hiding.<ref name=nk/> He joined the underground courier service Rolls Royce. One of his activities was to make contact from [[The Hague]] with already liberated parts of the Netherlands to exchange communication.<ref name=nk/> Van der Waals was caught by the authorities three times during the war-period, but managed to escape each time. Near the end of the war he went into hiding with family members living in the [[Veluwe]] region. When this area was liberated he was recruited as a translator for the [[Alsos Mission]] because he was able to speak German and English. In this capacity he was part of the liberation of [[Utrecht]] and saw the German technological facilities in [[Hook of Holland]].<ref name=nk/><ref name=mare/>

==Career==
After the war ended, Van der Waals finished his studies at the University of Amsterdam in October 1945.<ref name=nk/> He then started working for the [[Royal Dutch Shell|Koninklijke Shell]] Laboratorium Amsterdam.<ref name=mare/> He obtained his [[doctorate]] at the [[University of Groningen]] in 1950, with a thesis titled ''Thermodynamic Properties of Mixtures of Alkanes Differing in Chain Length''.<ref name=ul/> In the 1950s, Van der Waals developed insights in the description of clathrates and hydrates related to [[noble gas compound]], resulting in the 1959 Van der Waals–Platteeuw [[clathrate hydrate]] theory.<ref name=mare/><ref name=nk/> Van der Waals was appointed professor of experimental physics at [[Leiden University]] in 1967, and retired in 1989.<ref name=ul/> He specialized in [[molecular physics]].<ref name=mare/>

In 1962, Van der Waals received the [[Bourke Award]] of the [[Royal Society of Chemistry]].<ref>{{cite web|author= |url=https://www.rsc.org/ScienceAndTechnology/Awards/BourkeAward/PreviousWinners.asp |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190510122410/https://www.rsc.org/ScienceAndTechnology/Awards/BourkeAward/PreviousWinners.asp |title=Bourke Award Previous Winners |publisher=Royal Society of Chemistry |date= |archive-date=10 May 2019}}</ref> Van der Waals was elected a member of the [[Royal Netherlands Academy of Arts and Sciences]] (KNAW) in 1971.<ref>{{cite web|author= |url=https://knaw.nl/en/members/members/4963 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170821125705/https://knaw.nl/en/members/members/4963 |title=Joan van der Waals |publisher=Royal Netherlands Academy of Arts and Sciences |date= |archive-date=21 August 2017}}</ref> He served on the board of the KNAW between 1984 and 1987.<ref name=rvb>{{cite web|author= |url=https://magazines.rijksvastgoedbedrijf.nl/kei/2015/01/de-bewoners-hart-voor-het-pand |title=De Bewoners - Hart voor het pand |language=Dutch |publisher=Rijksvastgoedbedrijf |date= |accessdate=2 May 2020}}</ref> He has been an honorary member of the [[Royal Netherlands Chemical Society]] since 1998.<ref>{{cite web|author= |url=https://www.kncv.nl/leden/ereleden |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191211232239/https://www.kncv.nl/leden/ereleden |title=Ereleden |language=Dutch |publisher=Royal Netherlands Chemical Society |date= |archive-date=11 December 2019}}</ref> Van der Waals was appointed Knight in the [[Order of the Netherlands Lion]].<ref name=bio>{{cite web|author= |url=https://www.nederlandsekrijgsmacht.nl/index.php/kl/268-officieren-van-het-nederlandse-leger/manschappen-artikelen/artillerieofficieren/754-waals-joan-henri-van-der |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200502121403/https://www.nederlandsekrijgsmacht.nl/index.php/kl/268-officieren-van-het-nederlandse-leger/manschappen-artikelen/artillerieofficieren/754-waals-joan-henri-van-der |title=Waals, Joan Henri van der |language=Dutch |publisher=nederlandsekrijgsmacht.nl |date=1 October 2014 |archive-date=2 May 2020}}</ref>

Van der Waals has been involved in the conservation and restoration of the [[Trippenhuis]], the seat of the KNAW, since the 1980s.<ref name=rvb/>

==Personal life==
Van der Waals was married to Liesbeth van der Waals (1920–2014), with whom he had three children. In 1967 the pair separated.<ref>{{cite web|author=Frans Dijkstra |url=https://www.trouw.nl/nieuws/een-tweede-leven-met-vrouwen~b53a205f/ |title=Een tweede leven met vrouwen |language=Dutch |publisher=[[Trouw]] |date=3 March 2014 |accessdate=2 May 2020}}</ref> Van der Waals was the [[cousin twice removed|first cousin, twice removed]], of Dutch [[Nobel Prize]]–winning physicist [[Johannes Diderik van der Waals]].<ref name=mare/> He was an avid [[sailor]] and has made trips to the [[polar circle]] and [[Argentina]].<ref name=mare/><ref name=bio/>

Van der Waals [[centenarian|turned 100]] on 2 May 2020,<ref>{{cite web|author= |url=https://www.knaw.nl/nl/actueel/nieuws/felicitaties-voor-honderdjarige-knaw-lid-joan-van-der-waals |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200502175108/https://www.knaw.nl/nl/actueel/nieuws/felicitaties-voor-honderdjarige-knaw-lid-joan-van-der-waals |title=Felicitaties voor honderdjarige KNAW-lid Joan van der Waals |language=Dutch |publisher=Royal Netherlands Academy of Arts and Sciences |date=1 May 2020 |archive-date=2 May 2020}}</ref> and died on 21 June 2022, at the age of 102.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Voet |first1=Mel |title=Natuurkundige Joan van der Waals (1920-2022) bleef altijd scherp van geest |url=https://www.mareonline.nl/wetenschap/plots-ging-het-licht-schijnen/ |work=Mare |date=23 June 2022 |language=nl}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://images.nrc.nl/nOTuy_vCBOV3n9ureA0f_qb7ng0=/x/filters:no_upscale():format(jpeg):fill(f8f8f8,true)/s3/nrchub/clippings/NH/20220625/326-advertisement-244647_1297652_waals01-cae5c0.png |title=Death notice |publisher=NRC |access-date=25 June 2022 |language=nl}}</ref>
